question_text: A hypothetical metal has the BCC crystal structure, a density of $7.24 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{cm}^{3}$, and an atomic weight of 48.9 $\mathrm{g} / \mathrm{mol}$. What is the atomic radius of this metal?The unit of the answer is nm.
response:
For a BCC metal, the lattice parameter–radius relationship is $a = \dfrac{4R}{\sqrt{3}}$, and density is

$$\rho = \frac{nA}{a^3 N_A},\qquad n=2\ \text{(BCC)}$$

Solving for $a$:

$$a = \left(\frac{nA}{\rho N_A}\right)^{1/3} = \left(\frac{2(48.9)}{7.24 \times 6.022\times10^{23}}\right)^{1/3} = 2.82\times10^{-8}\ \text{cm}$$

Then

$$R = \frac{a\sqrt{3}}{4} = \frac{(2.82\times10^{-8})(1.732)}{4} = 1.22\times10^{-8}\ \text{cm} = 0.122\ \text{nm}$$

$$\boxed{0.122}$$
